title: Japanese Ukiyo-e
description: Woodblock prints of the 'floating world' — landscapes, kabuki, and everyday Edo life.

items.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura), also known as The Great Wave, from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei)"
items.description_narrative: This iconic woodblock print dramatically captures a towering wave about to engulf fishing boats, with the distant, snow-capped Mount Fuji serene on the horizon. It masterfully contrasts the raw power of nature with human vulnerability, characteristic of Hokusai's celebrated series.
items.tags: ukiyo-e, woodblock print, seascape, landscape, Mount Fuji, Japanese art, Edo period, nature

items.title: Cranes on snow-covered pine
items.description_narrative: Two elegant cranes stand gracefully amidst a serene, snow-covered pine landscape, their white plumage contrasting with the dark branches. This striking scene is brought to life through a color woodblock print by the renowned Katsushika Hokusai.
items.tags: japanese art, ukiyo-e, woodblock print, cranes, winter, nature, edo period

items.title: Shower Below the Summit (Sanka hakuu), from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjurokkei)"
items.description_narrative: This vibrant color woodblock print, 'Shower Below the Summit,' captures Mount Fuji amidst a dramatic storm. It is one of Katsushika Hokusai's iconic works from his renowned series, 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji.'
items.tags: mount fuji, landscape, storm, woodblock print, ukiyo-e, japanese, dramatic

items.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura), also known as The Great Wave, from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjurokkei)"
items.description_narrative: A monumental wave crests dramatically, its foamy fingers reaching towards three fishing boats threatened by the turbulent sea. In the distance, the snow-capped peak of Mount Fuji remains serene and small against the vast expanse.
items.tags: ukiyo-e, woodblock print, seascape, japanese art, landscape, wave, fuji

items.title: Hara, from the series ""Fifty-three Stations of the Tokaido (Tokaido gojusan tsugi)""
items.description_narrative: This color woodblock print by Hokusai captures 'Hara,' one of the key stops along the historic Tokaido Road. As part of his "Fifty-three Stations of the Tokaido" series, it offers a glimpse into the landscapes and journeys of Edo-period Japan.
items.tags: ukiyo-e, woodblock print, japanese landscape, travel, edo period, tokaido, hokusai

items.title: Kohada Koheiji, from the series "One Hundred Ghost Tales (Hyaku monogatari)"
items.description_narrative: This color woodblock print by Katsushika Hokusai depicts the ghost of Kohada Koheiji, floating menacingly from the series "One Hundred Ghost Tales (Hyaku monogatari)." Hokusai's masterful use of line and color brings to life the chilling atmosphere of this traditional Japanese ghost story.
items.tags: ghost, woodblock print, ukiyo-e, horror, japanese, supernatural, edo period

items.title: Komurasaki of the Miuraya and Shirai Gompachi (Miuraya Komurasaki, Shirai Gompachi)
items.description_narrative: This color woodblock print by Kitagawa Utamaro depicts the courtesan Komurasaki of the Miuraya and the outlaw Shirai Gompachi. Their story, popularized through kabuki theater, frequently appeared in Edo period art.
items.tags: ukiyo-e, woodblock print, Edo period, Japanese, courtesan, kabuki, drama, figures

items.title: Goldfish, from the series "Elegant Comparison of Little Treasures (Furyu kodakara awase)"
items.description_narrative: Kitagawa Utamaro's 'Goldfish' is a color woodblock print from his series 'Elegant Comparison of Little Treasures,' showcasing the artist's delicate touch. Executed in the oban format, this work reflects the artistry of early 19th-century Japanese printmaking.
items.tags: goldfish, woodblock print, ukiyo-e, japanese art, delicate, elegant, nature

items.title: Drawing Lots for Prizes (Ho biki)
items.description_narrative: This triptych by Kitagawa Utamaro is composed of three color woodblock prints, showcasing a scene of people engaging in a lottery for prizes. The expansive format allowed the artist to capture a lively gathering, characteristic of his work in portraying social activities.
items.tags: ukiyo-e, woodblock print, daily life, lottery, gathering, figures, Edo period

items.title: The Courtesan Arihara of the Tsuruya, and Child Attendants Aoe and Sekiya (Tsuruya uchi Arihara, Aoe, Sekiya), from an untitled series of courtesans
items.description_narrative: This vibrant color woodblock print by Kitagawa Utamaro depicts the courtesan Arihara of the Tsuruya, elegantly portrayed alongside her young child attendants, Aoe and Sekiya. The work highlights the intricate beauty and social conventions of the Floating World in late 18th-century Japan.
items.tags: courtesan, ukiyo-e, Edo period, woodblock print, Japan, portrait, genre scene

items.title: A Test of Skill - the Headwaters of Amorousness (Jitsu kurabe iro no minakami): Osan and Mohei
items.description_narrative: Kitagawa Utamaro's color woodblock print, titled "A Test of Skill - the Headwaters of Amorousness: Osan and Mohei," depicts two specific figures. As an example of the artist's prolific output, this oban print reflects the refined aesthetics of the Ukiyo-e tradition.
items.tags: ukiyo-e, woodblock print, Edo period, Japanese art, lovers, narrative, figure study
